# Part2D

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Part2D")`

A sprite and a body in one, on the 2D plane (the 2D layer, phase 3): what a `Part` is to a 3D world. It lies on the world's XY plane facing -Z, so an orthographic `Camera` looking down -Z sees it as it is; `ZIndex` orders sprites that overlap. It is drawn as its `Image` -- or a flat `Color` without one -- and simulated by 2D physics unless `Anchored`, which makes it ground.

**Members below are the ones this class DECLARES.** Everything its base
offers is on the base's page, which is what keeps one added member on
`Instance` from being a change to every page here.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Anchored` | `boolean` | — | read/write | Ground: it does not move, and what lands on it stays. A script may still move it. |
| `AngularVelocity` | `number` | — | read/write | Degrees per second, counter-clockwise. |
| `CanCollide` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether other parts bump into it. A part that cannot collide is only a picture. |
| `CollisionGroup` | `string` | `"Default"` | read/write | The group deciding which other parts it collides with, as `PhysicsService` names them. |
| `Color` | `Color3` | `Color3.new(1, 1, 1)` | read/write | Multiplies the image; with no image, the colour it is drawn in. |
| `Density` | `number` | `1` | read/write | Kilograms per square metre: with `Size`, how heavy it is. |
| `Elasticity` | `number` | — | read/write | How much of its speed a bounce gives back: 0 lands dead, 1 bounces for ever. |
| `Filter` | `Enum.TextureFilter` | — | read/write | Linear for painted art, Nearest for pixel art. |
| `FixedRotation` | `boolean` | — | read/write | Never turns, whatever hits it: a character that stays upright. |
| `FlipX` | `boolean` | — | read/write | Mirrors the picture left to right: a character facing the other way. |
| `FlipY` | `boolean` | — | read/write | Mirrors the picture top to bottom. |
| `Friction` | `number` | `0.3` | read/write | How much it grips what it slides on. Zero is ice. |
| `GravityScale` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How strongly `Workspace.Gravity` pulls it: 0 floats, 2 falls twice as hard, and a negative number falls up. |
| `Image` | `Content` | — | read/write | The picture, stretched over `Size`. Its transparent pixels are transparent. |
| `ImageRectOffset` | `Vector2` | — | read/write | The top-left of the part of the image drawn, in pixels: one frame of a sprite sheet. |
| `ImageRectSize` | `Vector2` | — | read/write | The size of that part in pixels. Zero on both axes draws the whole image. |
| `Position` | `Vector2` | — | read/write | Where its middle is, in metres. |
| `Rotation` | `number` | — | read/write | Degrees, counter-clockwise. A part with `FixedRotation` keeps whatever this is. |
| `Sensor` | `boolean` | — | read/write | Reports what enters it through `Touched` and pushes nothing: a coin, a checkpoint, a trigger. |
| `Shape` | `Enum.Shape2D` | — | read/write | The outline it is drawn and collides as. |
| `Size` | `Vector2` | `Vector2.new(1, 1)` | read/write | Width and height in metres: the picture's and the collider's. |
| `Transparency` | `number` | — | read/write | 0 is as drawn, 1 is invisible. A transparent part still collides. |
| `Velocity` | `Vector2` | — | read/write | Metres per second. Written by the simulation every tick, and a script may set it: a jump is setting its y. |
| `ZIndex` | `number` | — | read/write | Which of two overlapping sprites is in front: the higher. Ties keep the tree's order. |

## Methods

### `ApplyImpulse(impulse: Vector2)`

A sudden push, in kilogram-metres per second, at its middle. Applied at the next tick; an anchored part ignores it.

## Events

Every signal here is **deferred** (ADR 0015): a handler runs at the next
drain point, never inside the call that fired it.

### `TouchEnded(otherPart: Instance)`

Fires when something that was touching it stops.

### `Touched(otherPart: Instance)`

Fires once when something begins touching it -- another `Part2D`, or a `Tilemap2D`'s solid tiles -- or, for a `Sensor`, begins overlapping it. Deferred like every signal.
